description: Local transit. Lane A writes 1080p29.97 v210 in real time for 20 min, stamping mxlGetTime() into every payload. Lane B reads the same flow grain by grain with a blocking read and reports stamp.transit_ms = read wall clock - stamped write time; both ends are the same process, so the clocks are the same clock and the number is pure shared-memory propagation. Lane C is a once-per-second head probe that cannot desync, kept as a watchdog for the 20-minute run. Pair with 09-transit-remote-reader on the far host. Log with ABI_TESTER_LOG_FILE, then run mxl-transit-stats.py.

A.note: no "domain" key means the alias "default", i.e. whatever domain path the server was started with -- portable to the other host
two grains ahead of now, so the first paced write aims at a deadline that has not already passed
warm-up: the first OpenGrain in a process is an outlier
stamp:true writes magic+index+mxlGetTime() into the first 24 payload bytes; that timestamp is the only end-to-end reference a reader gets
marks the flow inactive, so the far end can see the run end

B.note: diagnostic only; the lane does not branch on it. is_active:false here means the flow has no writer in THIS domain yet
the first grain not yet written; every read after this blocks on the writer instead of racing it
blocking, so the loop is paced by the writer itself -- no delay_before_ms

C.note: always jumps to the newest committed grain, so this lane can never desync; its transit carries up to one commit interval of extra age

name: 08-transit-local
